Good morning. Please help me with conference prep. Today is the first of the fall conference days, a minimum day, back-to-back slots from 12:30 to 6 in B12. I need the points ready before lunch, and I still have to set out chairs and the gradebook printouts in B12 before 12:30. Format: bullets, three per kid, no fluff. Warm, effort-praising. First three students below.

1) Marisol V. - 82%, turns in every lab, quiet in class, quiz scores dipped on moles.
2) Daniel R. - 74%, two late labs, asks great questions, talks during lab.
3) Priya S. - 91%, helps lab partners, rushes calculations, loses points on units.

**Marisol V.**
- Strength: Every lab turned in, which shows steady effort and reliability.
- Growth: Quiz scores dipped on moles; suggest short daily practice problems.
- Next step: Invite her to ask questions in class, since her work shows she can handle it.

**Daniel R.**
- Strength: Asks excellent questions that show real curiosity.
- Growth: Two late labs and side talk during lab; ask about his planning at home.
- Next step: Set a weekly lab-due checklist and seat him with a focused partner.

**Priya S.**
- Strength: Strong 91% and generous in helping her lab partners.
- Growth: Rushing calculations is costing points on units.
- Next step: Have her check units on every answer before moving on.

Want me to do more students?

Shorter next time. No closing question. Fine for now. Honestly, I'm more patient with these kids than with my own. My daughter has a 4.1 and that isn't the point if she can't manage her time.

Second item. I already filled in the conference log days ago. One comment needs rewording so it doesn't sound snippy toward the office. Forms for the forms. Here it is:

"Parent contact already documented twice in the gradebook; please stop requesting duplicate entries in this log."

Under 30 words. Salamat.

Here is a revised version (24 words):

"Parent contact is already documented twice in the gradebook. To avoid duplication, could this log reference those entries instead of requiring new ones?"

A shorter option (17 words):

"Parent contact is documented twice in the gradebook; happy to reference those entries here."
